**About** **North Bay Regional Center**


North Bay Regional Center (NBRC), one of 21 regional centers located throughout California, is a private non\-profit (501(c)3\), started as a grass roots movement to assist persons with intellectual disabilities — and their families — in identifying and developing services and programs within their communities that help them lead more independent lives. The regional centers were established by the Lanterman Act (California Welfare \& Institutions Code §4500 *et seq.*) and are regulated by Title 17 of California’s Government Code. Regional centers serve as the point of entry into the State’s developmental services delivery system, providing life\-long services and supports to individuals with developmental disabilities and their families.


North Bay Regional Center was incorporated in 1972 and proudly serves the needs 13,000 children and adults with developmental disabilities in the linguistically and culturally diverse communities of Napa, Solano and Sonoma counties. NBRC is guided by a dedicated Board of Directors and supported by approximately 400 staff and 1,500\+ service providers. Our mission is to empower, respect and serve each child and adult with or with the potential for a developmental disability, while promoting the health and well\-being of each individual, their families, and our community.


We value:\~ Belonging \~ Compassion \~ Dignity and Respect \~ Honesty and Integrity \~ Humility \~**Servant Leadership is Ultimately an Act of Stewardship.**


At North Bay Regional Center, the Executive Director is entrusted with far more than the leadership of a complex organization. The Executive Director is entrusted with helping create the conditions in which individuals with developmental disabilities, families, employees, service providers, community partners, and future leaders can flourish together.


This opportunity calls for a leader who understands that operational excellence and human dignity are inseparable—that responsible stewardship of public resources, thoughtful leadership of people, and meaningful relationships all contribute to the same purpose: supporting individuals to live lives of their own choosing as valued members of their communities.


As North Bay Regional Center looks toward its next chapter, we seek a leader who is inspired by that responsibility and who believes, as we do, that leadership is ultimately measured not by authority, but by the opportunities it creates for others.

**Presbytery of Los Ranchos (PLR)** **Full\-Time \| Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (Flexible)** **Location: Must reside within the geographic bounds of the presbytery**

**Salary Range:** *$85,000 – $95,000 annually, depending on experience*

The Presbytery of Los Ranchos (PLR) is seeking a mission‑minded, highly skilled **Director of Operations** to provide leadership, continuity, and excellence across all operational and business functions of the presbytery. This role is central to ensuring the presbytery’s ministries are supported by strong financial stewardship, effective administrative systems, and well‑managed properties and resources.

**About the Role**

The Director of Operations oversees the operational life of the presbytery, complementing its mission and ministry work. This position is hands\-on and is responsible for a wide range of business functions, including accounting, financial reporting, human resources, benefits administration, payroll, property management and development, contracts, insurance, and office operations.

The Director reports to the **Executive Presbyter** and works closely with the **Trustees**, **Staff Relations Committee**, and the **Presbytery Treasurer**, while supervising the Assistant to the Director of Operations and coordinating with outside service providers such as CPA firms, payroll services, property managers, IT providers, and legal counsel.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Accounting \& Financial Management – 75%**

* Maintain QuickBooks general ledger and supporting accounts.
* Prepare, review, and track annual budgets.
* Manage accounts payable and check distribution.
* Prepare monthly financial statements, year‑end reports, audit documentation, and special reports.

**Human Resources \& Staff Relations\-15%**

* Process semi\-monthly payroll for all PLR employees.
* Ensure compliance with employment policies and state/federal regulations.
* Maintain and update the Manual of Operations for business functions.

**Office/Property Management\-10%**

* Collaborate with developers and property managers on valuations, redevelopment, repairs, and maintenance.
* Develop long‑term property plans that support congregational and presbytery mission.

**Qualifications**

* A committed follower of Jesus Christ with a passion for serving others.
* Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting **and** at least **five years of practical accounting experience**. Strong understanding of accounting standards.
* Minimum five years of recent, related experience—nonprofit experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to manage HR, operations, and outside service providers.
* Proficiency with SharePoint, Dropbox, Excel, Word, Adobe, Expensify, and related tools.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills; Korean or Spanish proficiency is a plus.

**Work Style \& Aptitude**

We’re looking for someone who:

* Works well independently and collaboratively.
* Prioritizes effectively and remains calm under deadlines.
* Demonstrates strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Shows initiative, problem‑solving ability, and a positive outlook.
* Offers insight and leadership without requiring close supervision.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

* Full‑time position with employer‑subsidized health care and retirement benefits.
* Flexible weekday schedule.
* Opportunity to serve as a role model and leader within a mission‑driven Christian organization.

**Additional Notices (California Compliance)**

**Reasonable Accommodation Statement:** PLR provides reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants with disabilities upon request, in accordance with California law.

**At‑Will Employment Notice:** Employment with PLR is considered at‑will, meaning either the employee or the presbytery may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice.

**Background Check Disclosure:** Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, conducted in compliance with California law.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should submit:

* A cover letter describing their interest and alignment with the mission of PLR
* A résumé highlighting relevant experience
* Contact information for three professional references

Applications may be sent to: **jobs@losranchos.org**

Pay: $85,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 403(b)
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Paid sick time
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Travel reimbursement
* Work from home

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Anaheim, CA 92805

**Director of Development**

**Position Type:** Regular, Full\-Time, Exempt, 12\-month

**Reports To:** Head of School (in close partnership with the Director of Community)

**Location:** Mount Madonna School, Watsonville, CA (on\-site, with occasional local travel for donor visits)

**Compensation:** Starting at $90,000 annually, plus performance\-based bonus tied to fundraising results; commensurate with experience

**Start Date:** Fall 2026

**About Mount Madonna School**

Founded in 1979, Mount Madonna School (MMS) is a co\-educational, preschool through grade 12, college\-preparatory day school nestled in the Santa Cruz Mountains straddling Watsonville and Gilroy. MMS is a diverse learning community dedicated to creative, intellectual, and ethical growth. We value each individual and all of their unique qualities – including race, culture, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, ability status, and socio\-economics – which weave into the tapestry of our shared humanity.

As a learner\-centered school, MMS has a rich tradition of innovative education that explores the potential of each student, balancing academic rigor with social\-emotional growth. MMS is accredited by the California Association of Independent Schools (CAIS) and the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC), and pursues its mission through the integration of Academic Excellence, Creative Self\-Expression, and Positive Character Development.

**Position Overview**

Mount Madonna School is creating a dedicated Director of Development position as part of a broader investment in the school's long\-term advancement capacity. Fundraising currently sits inside a single consolidated role alongside enrollment and marketing – a structure that has limited the school's capacity for the sustained, relationship\-based major gift work that MMS's leadership has identified as its highest\-leverage fundraising strategy. This newly defined position gives that work a dedicated, senior\-level owner for the first time.

The Director of Development will build and lead a comprehensive philanthropic program: major gifts, annual giving, institutional giving, and donor stewardship, in service of MMS's strategic priorities, including enrollment growth, program investment, and reduced reliance on ad hoc, one\-time sources of support. This role will work in close partnership with the Director of Community (enrollment and marketing) and report directly to the Head of School, ensuring fundraising strategy is fully integrated with the school's broader advancement and community\-building efforts.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a development professional who wants to build something durable: a philanthropic program with real infrastructure, an engaged and better\-utilized board, a reactivated alumni community, and a growing base of donors giving at meaningful levels, inside a mission\-driven, close\-knit school community with nearly 50 years of history.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership \& Planning**

* Develop and lead MMS's comprehensive fundraising strategy in alignment with the school's strategic plan and financial goals.
* Create an annual development plan with clear revenue targets, tactics, and timelines.
* Partner with the Head of School, Director of Community, and Board to identify funding priorities and shape the school's case for support.
* Establish metrics, tracking systems, and regular reporting to measure fundraising progress.

**Major Gifts \& Individual Donor Relations**

* Make relationship\-based major gift cultivation the center of the role – the deep, one\-on\-one work that the school's current staffing structure has not had capacity to sustain.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, with a focus on gifts of $5,000 and above.
* Build and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects among current families, alumni, grandparents, and friends of the school.
* Conduct regular donor visits and meetings (in person, phone, or virtual).
* Equip and coach board members to host small, informal cultivation gatherings for prospective major donors, extending the school's reach beyond staff capacity.
* Develop compelling gift proposals and agreements tailored to donor interests, in coordination with the Director of Community on messaging.
* Design and manage meaningful donor recognition and stewardship programs.

**Annual Giving \& Community Engagement**

* Lead MMS's annual giving program, transparently communicating the school's full funding need to the community and building a strategy that shifts emphasis toward fewer, larger gifts rather than broad, low\-yield participation pushes.
* Own the revenue outcomes for Drive for Schools and Summit for the Planet, MMS's two signature community fundraising events – partnering with the Director of Community on marketing and logistics, while holding accountability for the fundraising results.
* Own the success of MMS's community\-wide 100% giving (participation) campaign, ensuring every family, faculty, and staff member has a clear, low\-barrier way to participate.
* Build MMS's alumni engagement program essentially from the ground up – developing a real alumni database and re\-establishing relationships with a community that has been largely untapped to date.
* Plan and execute 1–2 signature donor cultivation and fundraising events each year, in partnership with the Advancement Coordinator.
* Develop peer\-to\-peer and special campaign fundraising initiatives.
* Partner with faculty and program staff to showcase student and school impact to donors.

**Institutional Partnerships**

* Research and identify foundation, corporate, and mission\-aligned funding opportunities.
* Write and submit compelling grant proposals and reports; manage the grant calendar and reporting requirements.
* Cultivate relationships with foundation program officers and institutional partners.

**Board Development**

* Staff the Board's Development/Advancement

That playful, bold spirit still thrives today, all on a campus renowned as among the most beautiful in the world.

Smarter Balanced is housed at the University of California, Santa Cruz (UCSC) Silicon Valley Extension.  

  

Our work is guided by the belief that a high\-quality assessment system can provide information and tools for teachers and schools to improve instruction and help students succeed, regardless of disability, language, or subgroup. We involve experienced educators, researchers, state and local policymakers, and community groups working together in a transparent and consensus\-driven process.

Developed with guidance from key industry leaders and academic experts, our certificate programs match the economic demand of your industry, from engineering to business, education to bioscience. Many of our courses may be applied toward degree programs or may be eligible for professional certificates and licenses.  

  

More information can be found at https://smarterbalanced.org

The Deputy Executive Director serves as the initial escalation point for office\- and organization\-wide risks and plays a key role in safeguarding organizational integrity through effective risk management, compliance oversight, and institutional accountability.  

  

The position provides executive oversight of core operational systems, including finance, human resources, production planning, and quality assurance, ensuring alignment with University of California and UC Santa Cruz policies and best practices. Through continuous improvement, performance monitoring, and strategic resource stewardship, the Deputy Executive Director strengthens operational effectiveness, drives efficiency, and ensures that Smarter Balanced products and services meet the highest standards of quality and reliability.  

  

As a senior leader, the Deputy Executive Director supervises and develops executive officers across External Affairs, Product and Strategy, Content, Psychometrics, Research, and Project Management. jobs.description:
Community Access was founded in 1974 to provide housing and support for people being discharged from psychiatric institutions. Today, we are one of the leading providers of supportive and affordable housing in New York City, and the originators of an integrated housing model which has become a best practice nationally: affordable housing where families live alongside people living with mental health concerns. Our staff work daily to support thousands of New Yorkers through supportive and affordable housing, peer\-driven residential crisis support programs, training, advocacy, supported education, mobile treatment and other healing\-focused services.

 **Program/Department Description**


Intensive Mobile Treatment (IMT) is an innovative, creative, trauma\-informed mobile practice model designed to provide treatment, rehabilitation and support services to individuals whose needs have not been met by traditional services. IMT participants interact with homeless services, criminal justice, and behavioral health service systems. IMT teams are hired, trained and funded to maximize flexibility and continuity of care for persons who historically have been poorly served.


Community Access’ IMT Teams serve individuals who are street homeless or living between institutional settings and housing. Team members work collaboratively with settings in which the participant is living and use assertive engagement strategies to proactively engage individuals in services. IMT team members share responsibility for the people they serve, helping individuals attain housing and other personal and safety goals that may be of a health, social, work or education nature.


IMT teams are multi\-disciplinary and include psychiatry, nursing, social work, peer specialists and other staff members offering rehabilitation, treatment and recovery support services. The team provides expertise in the areas of housing, substance use and harm reduction, criminal justice, peer support and behavioral health recovery. Based on their area of expertise, team members collaborate to deliver comprehensive, integrated and flexible services that are responsive to a participant’s choices, needs and goals. With a small staff to participant ratio, services are brought to the participant and offered in natural settings, 24 hours a day and seven days a week

The **IMT Assistant Program Director** is responsible for assigned administrative and management tasks and for the provision of direct services. * Licensed in New York State in Clinical Social Work (LCSW, preferred) or Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor (LMHC)
* Minimum of three (3\) years direct clinical experience with adults in a behavioral health setting
* Minimum one (1\) years supervisory or management experience preferred
* Knowledge of multi\-disciplinary mobile team experience, preferred
* Experience training, coordinating and evaluating the work of clinical and support staff preferred
* Demonstrated leadership skills, ability to work as part of a team and skill in communicating program goals and holding people accountable to reaching them.
* Ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Be creative and flexible.
* Able to show initiative and be responsible for follow\-through.
* Be skilled in conflict mediation/negotiation and have an assertive approach to problem solving.
* Available to work a flexible schedule, mornings, evenings and weekends in response to participant needs

Pacific Environment is a nonprofit organization dedicated to confronting our most urgent environmental issues by connecting local and global movements, catalyzing policy change, and inspiring action for the benefit of people and our planet. Together, we promote a healthy climate, reduce pollution, and conserve biodiversity for an equitable and thriving future. Learn more at www.pacificenvironment.org.

Building on more than thirty years of policy wins for the Pacific Rim's peoples, ecosystems, and climate, Pacific Environment has been campaigning to end fossil fuel use, including to get ships off fossil fuels. Our federal strategies include securing strong regulatory frameworks and legislation to achieve zero\-emission shipping on a timeline commensurate with the climate emergency; mobilizing congressional and public pressure on federal agencies and policymakers to adopt binding emissions standards and public investments; and engaging industry and maritime workers as partners in the transition to zero\-emission shipping — working with bodies such as the U.S. Coast Guard, MARAD, and the Federal Maritime Commission to align national maritime policy with a zero\-emission shipping future.

**Position**

Pacific Environment seeks an experienced Federal Policy Director to lead the organization's federal government affairs strategy on maritime shipping issues. This role is the organization's principal advocate before Congress and federal agencies — including the U.S. Coast Guard, Maritime Administration (MARAD), Federal Maritime Commission (FMC), EPA, and Department of Transportation — on policy priorities such as vessel emissions and fuel standards, port and vessel infrastructure investment, supply chain resilience, and maritime workforce and safety standards.



The Federal Policy Director will build and maintain relationships with congressional offices and committee staff, track and analyze relevant legislation and rulemakings, represent the organization in coalitions and public forums, and translate technical maritime policy into actionable advocacy strategy. This is a senior externally facing role requiring deep familiarity with the federal legislative and regulatory process and credibility with maritime policy stakeholders.



### **Key responsibilities**

**Legislative \& Regulatory Advocacy*** Serve as the organization's lead representative to Congress, federal agencies, and the Administration on maritime shipping policy.
* Develop and execute a federal advocacy strategy and annual policy agenda in coordination with organizational leadership.
* Track, analyze, and respond to relevant legislation, appropriations, and agency rulemakings (e.g., Coast Guard authorization, MARAD programs, FMC actions, EPA vessel emissions standards, IMO\-related federal implementation).
* Draft and deliver testimony, comment letters, position papers, one\-pagers, and talking points for policymakers and internal leadership.
* Build and sustain relationships with congressional members and staff, relevant committees (e.g., House T\&I, Senate Commerce), and agency officials.
* Work with congressional offices to shape, draft, and advance legislative proposals.
* Secure new bipartisan cosponsors for priority legislation and lead efforts to frame bill messaging for cross\-party audiences.
* Carry out various advocacy tactics such as grassroots organizing, traditional and digital outreach, engaging policymakers, in\-person mobilization tactics, etc.


**Coalition \& Stakeholder Engagement**



* Represent the organization in coalitions, working groups, and industry/NGO partnerships focused on maritime and shipping policy.

Understanding the US and global air\-launched strike missile market is imperative, as is maintaining close, seamless dialogue with Kongsberg counterparts in Norway to grow business both within the US and beyond. Periodic visits and briefings to foreign diplomats or their Defense, Air, or Naval Attaches (potential customers) will also be required. The Joint Strike Missile BD Director shall be the primary link and conduit between Kongsberg’s Missile and Aerostructures Division campaigns and operations in Norway and the US market on a day\-to\-day basis. This position will primarily focus on the Joint Strike Missile product line but will also provide support and assistance across the entire current and future missile portfolio.

	+ Grow a strong base of relationships within the US Air Force, US Navy and US Marine Corps aviation communities to ensure visibility and growth of the Joint Strike Missiles, while elevating existing relationships with existing customer offices and develop / foster relationships with other offices to increase advocacy and integration of the JSM into other platforms.
	+ Manage recurring Trade Show participation by ensuring participation in high payoff potential venues and ensuring Kongsberg displays reflect evolving focus of existing or targeted customer base.
	+ Support international capture efforts, when required, through actions such as briefing Foreign Embassy staffs based in the DC area on capabilities and program developments.

We produce world\-leading Remote Weapon Systems (RWS) for the US Army, Marine Corps, and allies at our Johnstown, Pennsylvania factory. We have delivered more than 20,000 PROTECTOR RWS to 28 countries. The National Advanced Surface\-to\-Air System (NASAMS) is a highly mobile and tailorable capability that protects the airspace of 13 countries and Washington, DC. In 2027, we will do final assembly, test, and sustainment of the Naval Strike Missile and Joint Strike Missile systems at a new factory in southern Virginia.


Join us, and you’ll be part of a high performing team that develops advanced technology solutions to protect people and critical infrastructure in countries around the world. Explore your potential and discover what your future could be with Kongsberg Defense \& Aerospace, Inc.


Kongsberg US seeks a Director of Business Development to support growth of our Missile Product portfolio in the US, specifically focused on the Joint Strike Missile (JSM). This candidate will be the primary interface between Kongsberg US and Kongsberg Norway for all current and future business and government customers in the US and FMS markets.


Successful applicants must be aggressive and adroit at fostering / growing customer relationships, to include engagements at senior levels of the US military and Congressional offices. Understanding the US and global air\-launched strike missile market is imperative, as is maintaining close, seamless dialogue with Kongsberg counterparts in Norway to grow business both within the US and beyond. Periodic visits and briefings to foreign diplomats or their Defense, Air, or Naval Attaches (potential customers) will also be required. The Joint Strike Missile BD Director shall be the primary link and conduit between Kongsberg’s Missile and Aerostructures Division campaigns and operations in Norway and the US market on a day\-to\-day basis. This position will primarily focus on the Joint Strike Missile product line but will also provide support and assistance across the entire current and future missile portfolio.

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

* + Reporting to the Kongsberg US Vice President for Business Development \& Strategy and closely coordinating with Kongsberg (Norway) Missile \& Aerostructures Division Vice President for Business Development, the applicant will lead, develop and execute a comprehensive business development strategy to maximize efficient growth and profitability within the US.
	+ Maintain strong relationships with all current, and prospective, US customers. Coordinate Quarterly Update / Status meetings with existing customers to maintain relationships and connectivity between division program management in Norway and customers.
	+ Manage relationship between Kongsberg and US Air Force and US Navy aviation training commands to ensure current operator/strike mission planner knowledge of specific weapon capabilities and most current CONOPs considerations are integrated into student curriculum and operational training.
	+ Participate in and facilitate (when necessary) relevant Program Management Reviews.
	+ Grow a strong base of relationships within the US Air Force, US Navy and US Marine Corps aviation communities to ensure visibility and growth of the Joint Strike Missiles, while elevating existing relationships with existing customer offices and develop / foster relationships with other offices to increase advocacy and integration of the JSM into other platforms.
	+ Manage recurring Trade Show participation by ensuring participation in high payoff potential venues and ensuring Kongsberg displays reflect evolving focus of existing or targeted customer base.
	+ Support international capture efforts, when required, through actions such as briefing Foreign Embassy staffs based in the DC area on capabilities and program developments.
	+ Identify and pursue new business opportunities, commercial as well as military, to include strategic partnerships, joint ventures, and contract acquisitions.
	+ Analyze market trends, competitive landscape, and emerging technologies to inform strategic decisions and positioning.
	+ Forge and maintain strategic partnerships, alliances, and collaborations with key stakeholders, including military services, government agencies, industry partners, and suppliers.
	+ Sales and Revenue Growth: Drive sales initiatives and revenue growth by identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, contracts, and programs.
	+ Identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies to ensure the successful execution of business development initiatives.
	+ Participate in full opportunity lifecycle process, from opportunity identification through proposal delivery and award.
	+ Work as part of the Kongsberg US Business Development team to identify areas of cross collaboration and provide inputs to the overarching US Strategic Plan.
	+ Maintain awareness and understanding of new technology development / platform development projects and manage communication of efforts to current /potential US customers and industry partners, as appropriate.
	+ Hands\-on attitude to work with a willingness to learn and develop.
	+ Self\-starter.
	+ A team player who works well in dynamic teams and in matrix\-style project organizations.
	+ Problem solver \- identifying and resolving problems in production as they arise.
	+ Collaborative, collegial and enthusiastic attitude towards work.
	+ A willingness to embrace Kongsberg’s corporate values of collaboration, determination, reliability and innovation.
	+ A willingness to travel, including internationally, and undergo training when required.

------------------------------

**Meet True Vet**  

**At True Vet Solutions, we believe no veteran should have to fight alone for what they already earned.**  

Every day in America, veterans walk away from disability benefits they qualify for, not because they don't deserve them, but because the system meant to serve them is slow, confusing, and built to wear people down. We exist to change that. We stand between the veteran and the system, and we do not stop until they receive every benefit they earned.  

We are a team of high\-empathy, high\-standards people doing work that actually matters. We answer the call when someone who served is at the end of their rope, and we turn it into an outcome that changes their life. The proof is in what our clients live:* Tens of thousands of veterans represented
* $350M\+ in lifetime benefits secured for the people who served
* 4\.9\-star client rating across 634 reviews

**Where we're going.** We are not building a small shop that helps a few hundred veterans a year. There are millions of veterans in this country leaving earned benefits on the table, and we intend to reach them. We are building the most trusted veteran advocacy organization in America, and we are building it fast. If you are looking for a ceiling, this is the wrong place. If you are looking for a mission big enough to spend a career on, and a company moving fast enough for you to grow into the leader you're capable of becoming, keep reading.  

**The mission of this role**  

As an Executive Director, you’ll lead the development and implementation of the organization’s strategic goals and initiatives, as well as oversee the daily operations ensuring efficient resource management and operational excellence.  

**Who this is for*** You are meticulous — you catch the details everyone else skips, every time.
* You carry exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.
* You can inspire and mentor team members while promoting professional development and continuous improvement.
* You take ownership — when something is unclear, you chase it down instead of waiting.

**What you'll own*** Lead the development and implementation of the organization’s strategic goals and initiatives.
* Oversee the daily operations, ensuring efficient resource management and operational excellence.
* Develop and maintain strong relationships with corporate, including partners, and the community.
* Drive financial performance by managing budgets, financial planning, and securing new funding opportunities.
* Representing the organization at community events, conferences, and networking opportunities to enhance its presence and reputation
* Ensure compliance with relevant regulations, policies, and standards to maintain the organization’s integrity and accountability.

**Requirements*** Available Monday–Friday, core hours in a U.S. time zone.
* Occasional weekends may be required.
* A Bachelor’s degree in Marketing or a Medical background is preferred.
* Proven experience in an executive leadership role with a strong understanding of strategic planning and organizational development.
* Strong decision\-making skills with the ability to think critically and solve complex problems.
* Reliable home internet and a quiet space to take calls.

**What makes a great fit*** Marketing or medical background.
* A history of taking a messy process and making it cleaner without being asked.

**What we offer you*** Daily coaching and real skill development, you will be sharper in six months than you have ever been
* A clear path to grow: we promote from within and invest in the people who invest in the mission
* A team that has your back, and a standard worth being held to
* Work that lets you end the day knowing you changed the life of someone who served

**Benefits*** Remote\-first work, from anywhere in the USA
* Employer\-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Paid time off and company\-wide holidays
* Hospitality experiences and team gatherings that make remote feel connected

**Our Core Values**  

Our values are the heart of this company. The right person for any role here recognizes themselves in each of them.  

**Empathy, Without Exception.** Every veteran is a person who served, not a case number. We lead with understanding and we hold that standard on the hardest days, in the longest calls, with the most frustrated client. Empathy is the one thing we will never trade away.  

**Remarkable Character.** We do right by veterans when no one is watching. We tell each other hard truths with care, accept them with humility, and keep our words and our actions pointed at the same goal.  

**Relentless Advocacy.** We fight for every benefit a veteran earned, and we do not quit when the system pushes back. It is us against the issue, never us against the veteran, and never each other.  

**Competitive Greatness.** We hold ourselves to an elite standard because the people who served deserve elite representation. We compound small improvements into outsized results, and we build each other into leaders along the way.  

**How to apply**  

If this is the mission you've been looking for, apply now. Tell us why this work matters to you, we read every one.  

True Vet Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. We hire for character and capability, and we welcome applicants of every background. Veterans and military spouses are strongly encouraged to apply.
